mechanism_narrative: The sharp drop in WORKPLACES at t-0w signals weaker commuting and fewer weekday trip chains; that reduction should pull RETAIL_REC down over the next four weeks because discretionary shopping is tied to on-trip purchases and after-work visits.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall below its last-4-week mean while WORKPLACES remains materially below the prior three-week level.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while TRANSIT remains deeply negative, more time spent near home substitutes for shopping trips and suppresses retail foot traffic, implying lower RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -35 for two consecutive weeks while RESIDENTIAL is above +5
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days despite TRANSIT remaining below -35 and RESIDENTIAL remaining above +5.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS after the t-1w trough should pull RETAIL_REC up with a short lag because outdoor leisure trips often generate nearby food and shopping visits within the same week or the following week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS turns upward by at least 5 points week-on-week after a decline
failure_condition: PARKS rises week-on-week but RETAIL_REC does not improve within the next 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both deteriorate together, it indicates a broad restriction or shock to mobility that reduces in-person shopping access; RETAIL_REC should fall over the next four weeks as that shock persists.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES fall by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or increases over the next 28 days despite simultaneous weekly declines in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained lift in GROCERY_PHARM reflects more frequent local errands and stock-up trips, which tends to spill over into adjacent retail visits and raise RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM remains above its recent mean but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-4-week mean within 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL rises while WORKPLACES falls, the city is shifting toward home-based routines that displace discretionary shopping trips; this should lower RETAIL_REC over the next month.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES drops below -20 while RESIDENTIAL rises above +5
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite simultaneous high RESIDENTIAL and depressed WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: A stabilization of TRANSIT near its current deep negative level, after the recent improvement from t-3w to t-0w, would indicate a settled low-mobility regime that keeps retail footfall suppressed; RETAIL_REC should remain lower over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rebounds within 7 days while TRANSIT stays near -40 and does not improve materially.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rebound in PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM after a soft retail week would indicate more multi-purpose local trips, which should feed into higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM both rise for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays below its last-4-week mean even as both PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM rise for two straight weeks.
